description: Findings judged real but not fixed by the task that found them. Read by the lead at each post-task review, and promoted into tasks/prd.json when worth doing. Not part of any task's brief: no role file or doc points subagents here.

conventions.status: open | check (may already be fixed) | promoted (to the prd task named in notes) | wontfix (reason in notes)
conventions.source: the task whose review found it, or the review that did

items.title: A film whose image-track Cues cannot be parsed has them re-read and warned about on every scan
items.notes: No marker for unreadable; image_cues stays NULL and loadSeen selects it again.

items.title: A seek inside a long-showing image cue pays the cue's whole age, uncapped
items.notes: Measured 0.3 MB and 0.04 s per second of age at 640x360; a 4K film costs more and is unmeasured. A cap would drop a cue on screen, so it needs a viewer-visible decision. Promoted to JS-089 (2026-11-12).

items.title: Helper-kill replacement check allows a replacement starting after the first missing segment
items.notes: TestAKilledHelpersChunk... only requires replacement.Start >= dead.Next (no duplicates). A replacement starting several segments after the first missing one passes if another job made the gap, so the 'from the first segment missing' property is not enforced.

items.title: TestMoreWorkersFinishTheFilmSooner drops the 3-worker case on fewer than 3 cores
items.notes: On a 2-CPU runner counts is reduced to {1,2} and the 3-worker measurement is logged as not measured. This is a case dropped for core count in a test that still exists; the replacement mechanism test runs 2 and 3 workers regardless of cores, so the replacement's verdict is unaffected.

items.title: Shown speed vs recorded speed uses a 25 percent tolerance
items.notes: TestAWorkersShownSpeedIsTheOneItRecordedAndHoldsAcrossAPause compares shown speed with the recorded value using before < recorded*0.75 || before > recorded*1.25. This is a comparison of two measured speeds with a bound; it is not in timing-bounds.txt. It is probably stable on a paused job, but it is not exact and was not exercised under load.

items.title: A sleep sets the pause-time speed baseline in the metrics test
items.notes: TestAWorkerReportsItsJobWhileItRuns (metrics_integration_test.go) sleeps 1 s after jobs pauses, scrapes the speed, sleeps 5 s, scrapes again and requires them equal to 1e-9. On a slow runner ffmpeg progress still in the pipe after the 1 s can change the speed between the two scrapes, which fails a right build. The comment says it is read 'by now'. Reading only.

items.title: QA runs every touched ffmpeg test under ffmpeg 6.1, not a sample
items.notes: JS-071 took four merge-queue runs: two fixture artifacts of ffmpeg 6.1 (sparse subtitle packets muxed ahead of their video) were found by CI, not by QA's 6.1 runs.

items.title: Worker's pre-store ownership check treats its own 5s timeout as an interruption, so an outage where connects hang cancels the job instead of waiting
items.notes: In upload(), the check runs under context.WithTimeout(ctx, lease/2). If Postgres is away in the form where connections hang (packets dropped, as can happen behind a Service during a switchover) rather than being refused or reset, the error is context.DeadlineExceeded. db.IsAway deliberately returns false for that, so the code takes the errInterrupted path: the job is cancelled and its ffmpeg stopp

items.title: Reap hold-off is process-local, so a reaper that missed the outage can still forget live workers
items.notes: reapHold is read from db.Of(pool).Recent(10s), which is set only when that process's own queries or connections fail. A reaper that sees no failure, for example an api replica whose idle connection survived or was replaced without an error, forgets workers whose locks died with the old primary before they take them again. items.title: /healthz no longer touches Postgres, so a replica with a permanently broken database stays Ready
items.notes: The probe was changed to return 204 with no database check, as the task asks. A replica whose database is permanently unreachable (bad credentials after a rotation, a wrong host) stays in service, and every request on it then waits in db.Retry with no upper bound except the client giving up. A cap on the wait, or a separate readiness signal such as 'away longer than N minutes', would be cheap.

items.title: A staged segment file is no longer removed when the final UPDATE fails for a non-outage reason
items.notes: In Worker.upload, os.Remove(name) moved after the UPDATE and only the IsAway error returns before it. A non-away error now leaves the file on disk until the job's working directory is cleaned up. Alternative: remove the file only on success or on errWaiting.

items.title: An idle api or stream replica logs nothing about an outage
items.notes: With no scanInterval set (the default), api and stream replicas run no periodic query. internal/db/outage.go logs 'Postgres is away' and 'Postgres is back' only from the tracer, which needs a failing query or connection. items.title: db.IsAway treats any net.Error as Postgres being away, so job.run marks non-database network errors as cancelled, not failed
items.notes: IsAway returns true for any net.Error, including S3 or segment-store timeouts. worker.run now adds `|| db.IsAway(err)` to the cancelled branch, so a store outage that returns a net error ends the job as `cancelled`. Such jobs are never refused, and viewers restart them without limit instead of seeing the last-attempt-failed protection. The same IsAway test would also start an outage tracker and pr

items.title: Stream-role subtitle, attachment and font reads are not wrapped in Retry
items.notes: Items.Source in subtitles.go (lines 72, 246, 336, 457) and transcode.FetchSubtitle, FetchSup and StartFonts use the pool directly. Auth now waits, so a request that starts while Postgres is away waits as intended. A request that passes auth just before the outage, or one started after a brief blip, gets s.fail 500 on the first failed query. This is the same 500 the task forbids for the stream role

items.title: /healthz no longer reflects the database at all, so a replica partitioned from Postgres stays in service
items.notes: /healthz now always answers 204. A single pod that permanently loses its path to Postgres (wrong DSN host, a network policy) is never taken out of service. db.Retry keeps its requests waiting until each client gives up. Alternative: fail /healthz only once db.Of(pool).Total() for the current outage exceeds a bound well above a switchover, such as 2 minutes. That would still satisfy the 'whole outa

items.title: Process-global sync.Map keyed by pool, and a tracker that learns only from failures
items.notes: db.Of(pool) looks the tracker up in a package-level sync.Map that Open fills and nothing removes. Every caller that was handed some other pool (tests, tools) silently gets a nil tracker that never says 'away'. Holding the tracker on a small wrapper type or in Server/Jobs/Worker fields would cost a few constructor changes and would make the missing-tracker case a compile error, not a silent no-op.

items.title: Worker logs an ERROR for a Postgres switchover it survives
items.notes: Any Postgres switchover or restart ends the worker's liveness connection. The worker logs at Error level 'the worker's liveness connection ended; its jobs go on, and it claims none until it holds the lock again and its row is there' (line 285), then at Info 'holds its liveness lock again ... its jobs went on'. Operators see ERROR lines for an event the build survives. Reading only.

items.title: Unwrapped api and stream writes can still answer 500 across a switchover
items.notes: requireAuth waits for Postgres (db.Retry on userByToken), but the handlers' own writes are not wrapped: Sessions/Playing/Progress and /Stopped/Ping (sessions.go), planPlayback writes (stream.go ~248-412), Transcode.Stop in DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings (stream role, transcode.go:181 -> jobs.go:243-249). items.title: Silent failures for abandoned requests also hide real errors from operators
items.notes: fail() now returns without any log whenever r.Context().Err() != nil, for every error and not only outage errors. A player that abandons a request after 10 seconds, and a request that fails for a bug (not Postgres), now both leave no 'request failed' line. Operators lose the diagnostic for real failures on abandoned requests. Reading only.
